name: rsync-sync
description: Sync PersonalClaw state between your machines with rsync over ssh, to any host you can already log into — a home server, a NAS, a VPS. No object store, no credentials beyond your existing ssh key. Shards are encrypted end-to-end by default, and secrets are excluded upstream so they never reach the host.
author: PersonalClaw

x-meta.label: SSH host
x-meta.help: The ssh destination, optionally with a user — e.g. nas.local or backup@nas.local. Leave empty to rsync to a local or mounted path instead (then only the path below is used). Only letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore are accepted.

x-meta.label: Sync root path
x-meta.help: Absolute path to the sync root ON THE TARGET (e.g. /srv/personalclaw-sync), or a local absolute path when no host is set. Supports ~ and $VARS for local paths. Leave empty to configure later — the transport stays idle until set.

x-meta.label: SSH port
x-meta.help: Port for the ssh connection. Ignored when no host is set.

x-meta.label: SSH identity file
x-meta.help: Optional path to a private key to use for this host. Leave empty to let ssh pick from your agent and ~/.ssh/config. The key itself is never read by PersonalClaw — only handed to ssh by path.

x-meta.label: Local working directory
x-meta.help: Where the local mirror and staging trees live on this machine. The mirror is what makes pulls incremental — rsync only transfers what changed.

x-meta.label: Command timeout
x-meta.help: Maximum seconds any single rsync invocation may run before it is killed and the cycle reports a retryable failure. Prevents a hung transfer from wedging the sync job.
